questions.stem: What is a temporary table in SQL?
options: A table that stores a refreshed query snapshot until explicitly dropped
A table created within a database session and available only during the lifetime of that session
A read-only copy of a production table
A view that dynamically fetches rows from base tables
A table stored in external cloud storage
questions.explanation: Temporary tables are created within a database session and are only available during the lifetime of that particular session.

questions.stem: What happens to a temporary table when the database session ends?
options: It is refreshed with the latest data
It is converted into a permanent table
It is automatically discarded, as if DROP TABLE had been run
It is archived to external storage
It becomes a materialised view
questions.explanation: After the session ends the temporary table is automatically discarded, the same as running DROP TABLE, so no permanent storage is consumed.

questions.stem: Which two characteristics distinguish temporary tables?
options: Encrypted and compressed
Partitioned and indexed
Replicated and versioned
Session-specific and volatile
Persistent and scheduled
questions.explanation: Temporary tables are session-specific (visible only within the session that created them) and volatile (automatically deleted at the end of the session).

questions.stem: What kind of data are temporary tables designed to store?
options: Long-term compliance archives
Top-rated product lists for a website
Master reference data
Pre-aggregated reporting figures
Intermediate results, results of window functions for complex calculations and massive data manipulations
questions.explanation: Temporary tables store intermediate results, results of window functions for complex calculations or data processing tasks, and massive data manipulations.

questions.stem: How does a materialised view differ from a temporary table in terms of persistence?
options: A materialised view is stored in the database until explicitly dropped, whereas a temporary table is discarded at session end
A materialised view disappears at session end, whereas a temporary table persists
Both are discarded at the end of the session
Both persist until the database is restarted
A materialised view exists only in memory
questions.explanation: Unlike temporary tables, materialised views are stored in the database until a command is explicitly run to drop them.

questions.stem: How can a materialised view be refreshed?
options: Only automatically on every insert
On a schedule or on a manual basis
Only when the session restarts
Only by dropping and recreating it
It can never be refreshed
questions.explanation: Materialised views can be configured to refresh on a schedule or manually, ensuring data is up to date as needed.

questions.stem: For which type of workload do materialised views significantly improve performance?
options: Write-heavy transactional inserts
Schema migrations
Read-heavy operations, by precomputing and storing the query result
Session-specific personalisation
Backup and restore jobs
questions.explanation: Materialised views improve performance for read-heavy operations by precomputing and storing the query result.

questions.stem: In a data warehousing project, how are materialised views and temporary tables typically divided?
options: Materialised views hold raw source extracts; temporary tables hold final reports
Both are used only for backups
Temporary tables replace the ETL process entirely
Materialised views pre-aggregate data for reporting tools, while temporary tables handle intermediate manipulation during ETL
Materialised views are used only in web applications
questions.explanation: Materialised views pre-aggregate data for fast access by reporting and analytics tools, while temporary tables are used during ETL for intermediate data manipulation.

questions.stem: In a web application, which construct would store frequently accessed data such as top-rated products?
options: A temporary table
A session variable
A window function
A cursor
A materialised view
questions.explanation: In web applications, temporary tables handle session-specific processing such as personalising content, while materialised views store frequently accessed data like top-rated products.

questions.stem: Which statement about temporary tables is NOT correct?
options: They remain in the database until explicitly dropped by a command
They are visible only within the session that created them
They help avoid repeated calculations or data retrieval operations
They are useful for holding data without affecting the main database tables
They are supported by most modern RDBMS such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle and SQL Server
questions.explanation: Temporary tables are volatile and discarded automatically at session end; it is materialised views that persist until explicitly dropped.
